title: spec(notification): the push device registry's protocol face and the push payload route (spec slice of #29041)
body:
domain:server#5 · os-project-manager · session_01FEkQ5oc56xChD6Wrc4cGSt

Filing gate: the `packages/spec/**` slice of #29041 (p1, triage 2026-11-02 「协议新增定 p1」), split off by `domain:server` seat 5 so that no server dev order carries a spec hunk. The server runtime slices are blocked on this card. Graded p1, the same as its parent (a protocol addition: new served routes, a new system object, a new channel's payload contract). Graded under 「定级你可以自己决定」 (Leehom, 2026-11-01). Contract review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` is owed (declaration face).

Reach: the mobile shell (objectstack-ai/mobile#144) and the Console (#29042), which register a native APNs/FCM token under the signed-in session; authors of `notify` flow nodes whose deliveries go to phones.
Reader who acts: the `domain:spec` seat.

## What is there on `main`

- `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` still exports `RegisterDeviceRequestSchema` (`token`, `platform: ios|android|web`, optional `deviceId`, `name`), `RegisterDeviceResponseSchema`, `UnregisterDevice*` and the `*Preferences*` schemas, as protocol-method contracts with no route.
- `DEFAULT_NOTIFICATION_ROUTES` (`packages/spec/src/api/plugin-rest-api.zod.ts` ~line 1205) lists only list/read/read-all. Its comment records why the device and preference rows were removed (#3899, #3612): they were declared but never built.
- `INotificationService` (`packages/spec/src/contracts/notification-service.ts`) has no device member.
- `NotificationChannelSchema` (`system/notification.zod.ts`) names `push`, and its JSDoc says no channel delivers it.
- ADR-0012 §6 sketches `UserDeviceSchema` (`user_id`, `device_id`, `vendor`, `token`, `app_id`, `platform`, `locale`, `enabled`, `invalidated_at`, `last_seen_at`). §10 puts it in `notification/device.zod.ts`, and §11 puts `sys_user_device` under the push plugin.

## Wanted (the protocol face only, ⛔ no runtime)

1. **Device registration contract.** Revise or replace `RegisterDeviceRequestSchema` / `UnregisterDevice*` so that one request registers or refreshes a device for the current user. It carries `vendor` (`apns` | `fcm` in core; ADR-0012 routes HMS, Xiaomi, OPPO and vivo to plugins), `token`, a client-generated `deviceId` that is stable per app install, `platform`, an optional `appId` and `locale`. The response names the device. The removed fields' disposition goes under ADR-0087 if any field an author can write changes.
2. **Route rows.** Restore the device routes in `DEFAULT_NOTIFICATION_ROUTES` (register/refresh and unregister, under `/api/v1/notifications/devices`), with request and response schemas. Preferences stay out (not asked for).
3. **The stored device shape.** A `UserDeviceSchema` per ADR-0012 §6, narrowed to what core ships. State:
   - (a) whether a device row belongs to a user or to a user and an organization;
   - (b) that a token registered by a second user moves to that user (one live owner per token);
   - (c) the invalidation fields (`enabled`, `invalidated_at`).
4. **`INotificationService` device members** (register, unregister, list for a user, invalidate by token), as optional members so that existing implementations stay valid.
5. **Push payload contract.** A push delivery carries a Console `route` (for example `/apps/crm/opportunity/123`): a relative path only, and an absolute or off-server URL is refused or dropped at the contract. State where it comes from: an explicit notify key, or derived from the node's existing `sourceObject` / `sourceId`. Prefer derivation if it needs no new authorable key.
6. **Push transport configuration.** An APNs (token auth: team id, key id, topic/bundle id, sandbox or production, the `.p8` key by `credentialRef`) and FCM HTTP v1 (project id, service-account JSON by `credentialRef`) config shape. Secrets go only by reference (ADR-0143 D3), never inline. Place it where per-environment email transport selection lives, or say why not. If hosted environments need a cloud-side surface, that half goes to `domain:cloud` (triage note on #29041).
7. Update `NotificationChannelSchema`'s JSDoc once a server slice registers `push` (that can ride the server slice; name the hand-off).

Tests: schema round-trip and refusal cases (an off-server `route`, an unknown vendor, an inline secret), and the route catalog test that pins `DEFAULT_NOTIFICATION_ROUTES`.

Declarations: a widening (`Clause-②: yes`). `Metadata-protocol` per what changes; ADR-0087 disposition if any published field is renamed or removed.

Blocked-by: none.
Blocks: the server device-registry slice (filed beside this card) and #29041 (push channel).

Dedupe: searched `device registry spec push token route`, `RegisterDeviceRequestSchema`; only #29041 and #29042. **New.**

Links back: #29041, #29042, ADR-0012 §6 / §10 / §11, ADR-0143 D3.
